experimental_procedure: 1. Synthesis of 1,3,5-Br3-2-ClC6H2 (16) A 500 mL, two-necked, round-bottom flask fitted with a dropping funnel was charged with 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (3.30 g, 10 mmol) and hydrochloric acid (6M, 65 mL). The mixture was stirred on an ice bath for 20 min. Afterwards, to the suspension, was added drop-wise a solution of sodium nitrite (1.04 g, 15 mmol) in water (50 mL) and the mixture was stirred on the ice bath for 1 h. Copper(I) chloride (2.97 g, 30 mmol) was added in small portions with vigorous stirring. After the addition ended, the mixture was stirred for 30 min on an ice bath and 30 min at rt. The mixture was extracted with diethyl ether (4x15 mL). The organic fractions were combined and dried over Na2SO4. Filtration and evaporation of the solvent gave 3.21 g of brown solid. This product was sublimed at 70 °C (4x10-2 mbar) to give 16. Slightly yellow solid, yield 2.49 g, 71 %. Mp 92 - 94 °C (91 °C lit.);2 1H NMR (CDCl3, 300 MHz): δ 7.73 (s, 2H); 13C NMR (CDCl3, 75 MHz): δ 135.22 (s), 124.14 (s), 120.62 (s).

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Reactions of diazonium salts with KCl. General procedure. To a dispersion of 149 mg (2 mmol) of finely ground KCl in 1 ml of dry MeCN was added at stirring 0.1 mmol of a phase-transfer catalyst, 9.9 mg (0.1 mmol, 10 mol%) of CuCl, and 13.4 mg (0.1 mmol, 10 mol%) of CuCl2. After that 0.1 mmol (10 mol%) of ligand was added. After 30 min of stirring was added dropwise a solution of 1 mmol of diazonium salt I in 1-2 ml of dry MeCN, the obtained mixture was stirred for 1 or 24 h at room temperature or 1 h at 50°С, the reaction progress was monitored by GLC or 19F NMR spectroscopy. On the completion of the reaction the reaction mixture was poured into 50 ml of ethyl ether and passed through celite to remove the inorganic salts. The solvent was evaporated in a vacuum, and the residue if necessary was purified by column. chromatography IIc, yield 83%

authors: Honraedt, Aurelien; Gallagher, Timothy
reference: Concise Entries to 4-Halo-2-pyridones and 3-Bromo-4-halo-2-pyridones | Honraedt, Aurelien; Gallagher, Timothy | Synlett (2016), 27(1), 67-69
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the synthesis of 7b-c, 7e and 7f. To a mixture of copper source (1.2 eq., CuBr2 for 7b and 7c, CuCl2 for 7e, CuI for 7f) in acetonitrile (0.4M) was slowly added tBuONO (1.5 eq.). The mixture was stirred for 15 min and then cooled to 0°C. A solution of 2-benzyloxy-3-bromo-4-aminopyridine 7d (1.0 eq.) in acetonitrile (0.5M) was slowly added. The mixture was stirred for 1h at 0°C and then allowed to warm to r.t. for 16h. After concentration under reduced pressure, aq. 15% ammonia solution (2 mL/mmol) was added, and the aqueous layer was extracted with dichloromethane (5 mL/mmol; 3x). The combined organic layers were washed with brine, dried (Na2SO4), filtered and concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude was purified by flash chromatography on silica gel to give the product(s) 7b-c, 7e and 7f. 4-Benzyloxy-3, 4-bromopyridine 7b and 4-benzyloxy-3, 4, 5-tribromopyridine 7c Carried out on 1.0 mmol scale. Purification by flash chromatography on silica gel (hexane/DCM: 75/25) first yielded 4-benzyloxy-3, 4, 5-tribromopyridine 7c (141 mg, 33%) as a colorless solid. 4-Benzyloxy-3-bromo-4-chloropyridine 7e Carried out on 1.0 mmol scale. Purification by flash chromatography on silica gel (hexane/DCM: 70/30) gave 7e (256 mg, 86%) as a pale yellow solid. mp: 53-54°C (toluene); 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3,) δ 7.97 (d, 1H, J = 5.4 Hz), 7.50-7.48 (m, 2H), 7.41-7.37 (m, 2H), 7.34-7.30 (m, 1H), 7.00 (d, 1H, J = 5.4 Hz), 5.47 (s, 2H); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) δ 161.0, 145.7, 145.0, 136.6, 128.4 (2C), 127.9, 127.5 (2C), 118.9, 108.1, 69.0; IR (neat): 1567, 1539, 1438, 1411, 1336, 1035, 996, 753, 699 cm-1; HRMS (ESI+) Calcd for C12H10 79Br35ClNO [M+H]+: 297.9629; Found: 297.9630.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Reactions of diazonium salts with KCl. General procedure. To a dispersion of 149 mg (2 mmol) of finely ground KCl in 1 ml of dry MeCN was added at stirring 0.1 mmol of a phase-transfer catalyst, 9.9 mg (0.1 mmol, 10 mol%) of CuCl, and 13.4 mg (0.1 mmol, 10 mol%) of CuCl2. After that 0.1 mmol (10 mol%) of ligand was added. After 30 min of stirring was added dropwise a solution of 1 mmol of diazonium salt I in 1-2 ml of dry MeCN, the obtained mixture was stirred for 1 or 24 h at room temperature or 1 h at 50°С, the reaction progress was monitored by GLC or 19F NMR spectroscopy. On the completion of the reaction the reaction mixture was poured into 50 ml of ethyl ether and passed through celite to remove the inorganic salts. The solvent was evaporated in a vacuum, and the residue if necessary was purified by column. chromatography IIf, yield 87%
